methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece explicitly diagnosing how AI data center infrastructure concentrates in NoVA while exacerbating urban-rural divides—signals recognition of concentration without evidence of distributed capability-building response.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches online workforce training program - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Online workforce training expanding access beyond metro centers suggests distributed capability development, though 'on-demand' platform model may indicate shallow rather than deep skill acquisition.

signals.title: Norfolk Southern deploys AI system to catch wheel defects before they break - The Business Journals
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Southern deploying sophisticated AI defect detection demonstrates deep technical implementation in Hampton Roads industrial sector, but concentrated in single major corporation rather than distributed ecosystem.

signals.title: U.Va. pilots three new artificial intelligence literacy courses - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: UVA piloting AI literacy courses across student population signals institutional investment in broad-based capability development, though impact depends on whether learning emphasizes conceptual depth or surface-level tool use.

signals.title: Mahoney and Cronkhite: The co-investing, pro-bono partnership that won millions in grants for Appalachian communities
signals.signal_reading: UVA students providing pro-bono technical assistance to Appalachian communities for grant-writing demonstrates knowledge transfer mechanism that could distribute capability to historically underserved regions, though sustainability beyond student projects remains uncertain.
